description:
PharmacyOS is the retail-management system a Bangladeshi pharmacy runs its counter on — point of sale, inventory by batch and expiry, prescriptions, suppliers, and NBR-compliant receipts. This connector gives the owner and staff of one pharmacy a plain-language way into their own live records.

Ask what sold last month and get the real figure, with the count, discounts, VAT and total. Ask what is running out and get the items at or below their reorder level, with a suggested quantity to cover the next fortnight. Ask who owes money and get the khata book, biggest debt first, with each customer's remaining credit. Ask what money is stuck on the shelf and get the stock that has not sold in ninety days, valued at cost. Ask about one receipt by the number printed on it and get every line, the cashier, the discount, the VAT and the customer. Ask what you actually made and get gross profit and the month's operating expenses side by side.

With the owner's opt-in it also writes: create a medicine, change a price or a reorder level, receive a batch with its expiry, log rent or a salary, add a supplier, raise a draft purchase order, record a customer's payment against what they already owe, and save a photographed supplier invoice as a review session the owner finishes in the app.

Everything is scoped to the single pharmacy the signed-in user belongs to. There is no parameter on any tool that could reach another business's data, and no way to ask for one.

It is a business tool, not a clinical one. There is no drug monograph, indication, dose, interaction or therapeutic-equivalence information in any response, and no tool that provides any. Clinical questions belong with the pharmacist.

Amounts are in Bangladeshi Taka, held as integer paisa. Dates are Asia/Dhaka. Bangla and English both work.

defaultPrompt: What's running out, and how much should I order?
